minimum_questions: Confirm edition and artist identities; classify original recording versus reissue/remix/compilation.
Find or reuse one explicit musically meaningful geographic relationship: formation, professional scene, recording or documented repertoire. Current profile location alone does not meet this goal.
Inspect available edition/master recording credits; keep partial, ambiguous and unmatched credits qualified.
Assess source coverage and contradictions; record why further research would or would not change a published claim.
source_routing: Discogs for every edition; artist/label or an institutional/specialist source for context. Archive work is required for an unresolved historical claim, an identity conflict, vague reissue credits or a sample/heritage assertion. A decisive first-party source may close the archive route for a narrow question, with the cited reason recorded.
stop_rules: Stop the core context search after explicit primary evidence answers its narrow question, while retaining independent session questions.
For an unresolved question inspect one relevant primary/archival lead and a targeted alternative. If both fail to establish the detail, stop as bounded_unresolved; do not invent a location.
One corroborated relationship does not establish complete musical history.
Reopen bounded cases when a new source, contradiction or edition creates a reason to do so.
timing: Record source collection timestamps and elapsed HTTP operation time; measure overall batch wall time separately from unique requests. No extrapolation from coding time or parallel request durations to human review effort.
quality_goal: A completed review can retain unresolved facts. Report review completion, evidence usefulness and remaining limits separately.
